title: Late-Time Power Laws in Fluorescence Decays: Quantum Decay or Alternative Mechanisms?
authors: Francesco Giacosa, Anna Kolbus, Krzysztof Kyziol, Magdalena Plodowska, Milena Piotrowska, Karol Szary, Arthur Vereijken
abstract: In quantum mechanics, the properties of an unstable system are closely related to its corresponding energy distribution. One of the predictions of the theory is the emergence of a late-time power law in the survival probability $P(t)$ of the unstable state. However, in complex systems, similar effects may emerge due to other phenomena. This is the case for nonextensive statistical models, for some continuous lifetime distribution models, and also for certain energy-migration models applied to fluorescence. In this work, these alternative interpretations are confronted with data from time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy experiments with erythrosine B and eosine Y as fluorophores. It turns out that some of the features expected within the quantum-mechanical description, such as the sharp transition from the exponential to the power-law regime, cannot be reproduced by the specific statistical and energy-migration parametrizations fitted in the analysis.
summary: This paper examines the origin of late-time power-law tails in fluorescence decay, comparing predictions from quantum mechanics against alternative models like nonextensive statistics and energy migration. Using time-resolved spectroscopy data, the authors argue that the experimental features do not align perfectly with the predictions of these alternative models, lending support to a specific interpretation of the quantum decay process.
main_problem: The paper investigates the origin of late-time power-law decays observed in fluorescence decay curves, determining if they arise from fundamental quantum mechanical predictions or from alternative physical mechanisms.
main_result: The analysis suggests that the specific features expected from the quantum-mechanical description, such as a sharp transition from exponential to power-law decay, cannot be reproduced by the alternative statistical or energy-migration parametrizations fitted to the experimental data.
method: The authors compare time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy data from fluorophores (erythrosine B and eosine Y) against predictions from quantum decay theory, nonextensive Tsallis statistics, and energy-migration models.
model_or_system: The study uses time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy on molecular fluorophores. Theoretical models include standard quantum mechanical decay, Tsallis q-exponential relaxation, and energy-migration rate equations.
key_observables: The primary observables are the fluorescence intensity decay $I(t)$ and the power-law exponent ($ eta$) observed at late times.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the Tsallis nonextensivity index ($q$), the energy-migration rate parameters ($\gamma, 	au_2$), and the decay time constants ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed power-law decay must be explained by one of the tested theoretical frameworks, though the authors note that the ill-conditioned nature of the inverse problem limits uniqueness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the successful fitting of experimental data for Erythrosine B and Eosine Y using the Tsallis-statistics model and the energy-migration model, while contrasting these fits with predictions from the delayed fluorescence model.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical context of power-law decay in quantum systems, presents the experimental data from fluorescence spectroscopy, and then systematically confronts the QM predictions against alternative models (Tsallis, energy-migration) using fitting procedures.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interpretation of non-exponential decay in open quantum systems, a core topic in AMO physics and quantum optics, by rigorously testing competing physical models against real experimental data.
